verdict.rationale: LangGraph ships an official CLI that builds and runs the Agent Server locally from a terminal. That server exposes run, thread and assistant API endpoints, so an agent could drive a graph headlessly and check the results. The evidence never shows the CLI running the framework's example agents directly, or a one-shot terminal run-and-verify flow; it only shows a local server whose endpoints must then be called. Missing for 10: documented example agents runnable from the CLI, a direct headless run command with output for verification, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can run the framework's example agents headlessly from a terminal so an agent can verify what it just built

citations.quote: LangGraph CLI is a command-line tool for building and running the Agent Server locally.
The resulting server exposes all API endpoints for runs, threads, assistants, etc., and includes supporting services such as a managed database for checkpointing and storage.
